sentence_stem: Never before in the history of the company
correct_completion: has such a bold strategy been attempted.
full_sentence: Never before in the history of the company has such a bold strategy been attempted.
acceptable_variants: has a more ambitious plan ever been proposed.
has any board ever approved such a daring plan.

options.text: the board had attempted a bold strategy.
options.why_wrong: After a fronted negative phrase such as 'never before', English requires subject-auxiliary inversion. Normal word order here sounds unnatural and loses the rhetorical emphasis.

options.text: has such a bold strategy been attempted.
such a bold strategy was attempted by staff.
options.why_wrong: The fronted negative requires inversion of the auxiliary and subject, so 'was attempted' with normal word order is incorrect here.

options.text: the company has often tried bold strategies.
options.why_wrong: This removes the negative sense that the fronted phrase creates, so the rhetorical effect of emphasis is lost.

grammar_focus: Subject-auxiliary inversion after fronted negative adverbials
explanation: After a fronted negative adverbial, English requires inversion of the auxiliary verb and the subject. Learners may keep the normal subject-verb order, a common pattern when the first language allows relatively free word order and has no equivalent inversion rule for emphasis.
translation: Nunca antes en la historia de la empresa se ha intentado una estrategia tan audaz.
